thread:
megan: Hey team, ZetaCorp is seeing a burst of 429s last night around 03:10-03:15 UTC. They say their traffic didn't change. Can someone help triage? :grimacing:

tom: I'm looking now. Which pool/region? customer reports 'eu-west-1' in the ticket.

raj: Can you paste a sample of the 429 response headers from the customer's logs? that usually tells us whether it's rpm or tpm hitting.

megan: Here's a snippet they captured (redacted IDs):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2026 03:12:07 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: r-XXXX
X-RateLimit-Limit-RPM: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining-RPM: 0
X-RateLimit-Limit-TPM: 14400
X-RateLimit-Remaining-TPM: 350
{
  "error": {"message": "rate limited", "code": 429}
}
```

sophie: That looks like RPM is exhausted (Remaining-RPM=0) while TPM still has headroom. Could be a short fanout or a cron bunching at the minute boundary. Any cron windows for ZetaCorp?

megan: They say no cron. They do have ~200 concurrent clients using streaming sockets. 

raj: Two quick checks: 1) confirm per-tenant rpm time series for the 5m window, 2) check edge logs for bursty simultaneous connections. Run: 
```
infra-bot: redwood infra query --tenant zeta-corp --metric requests_per_minute --from 2026-03-10T03:05Z --to 2026-03-10T03:20Z --agg max
```

infra-bot: Query started... returning aggregates. Max RPM observed = 1,230 at 03:12:00Z. Baseline before spike ~320 RPM.

tom: That matches the headers. Their RPM limit is 1000 on the hosted plan. They hit a short spike to 1,230 which created 429s for concurrent requests.

sophie: Action items: (a) tell customer where the spike came from (client-side multiplexing?) (b) suggest immediate mitigations (graceful backoff + jitter), (c) consider temporary quota increase if business-critical.

megan: ZetaCorp is asking for a quick workaround they can push without code changes. Anything we can flip on our side?

raj: We can enable short-term ingress smoothing for that tenant (throttle smoothing / burst window expand) for up to 10 minutes while they implement client backoff. Ops will need approval.

ops-bot: Requested: temporary RPM burst allowance +20% for tenant zeta-corp for 10 minutes. Pending approval from @sophie and @tom.

sophie: Approved. ops-bot please apply and confirm. Also send ZetaCorp recommended client retry guidance: exponential backoff starting 200ms, jitter, and max concurrency of 60 per tenant token.

ops-bot: Applied at 03:14:30Z. New soft RPM limit = 1200 for 10m. No downstream config changes.

megan: Customer confirmed errors immediately dropped after ~30s. They want a root cause though — what triggered the spike?

raj: We saw a ~2x increase in open streaming sessions from a particular IP subnet at 03:11Z. Likely a bot/worker restart that reconnected many clients simultaneously. Recommend: (1) client side: stagger reconnects, use exponential reconnect; (2) server side: use connection token bucket to smooth reconnections; (3) for future: consider per-token concurrency caps + telemetry anomaly alerts.

tom: I'll file a follow-up ticket to add an automated alert when tenant RPM exceeds 80% of limit for >30s (so support gets early heads-up).

megan: Thanks all — I'll reply to ZetaCorp with the mitigation steps and timeline. :white_check_mark: If they ask for a permanent limit increase, route to account mgmt.

sophie: One-liner for the customer reply we can reuse: "We observed a short spike in concurrent requests that exceeded your per-minute allowance (1000 RPM). We temporarily raised your soft cap and strongly recommend implementing staggered reconnects and exponential backoff to avoid future 429s. We'll follow up with telemetry and options for a permanent quota change."

megan: Copying that into the ticket. Closing this thread once customer confirms.
